ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure gives three open-loop frequency responses/Nyquist curves side by side, labeled System1, System2, and System3 respectively. Each graph has complex-plane coordinate axes, the key real-axis points -1 and 0 are marked on the horizontal axis, and the frequency direction is indicated with arrows. The annotation of System1 is P=1, ν=0; the curve starts from near the negative real axis, winds downward into an arc, and then tends toward 0; looking at the complete Nyquist curve, it gives an encirclement of the -1 point that matches P=1. The annotation of System2 is P=1, ν=1; the curve is near the imaginary axis and bends leftward, but the encirclement situation relative to the -1 point does not satisfy the Nyquist winding number required when P=1. The annotation of System3 is P=0, ν=1; the curve passes in a wavelike form near -1, but the net winding number is 0, matching P=0. Then reason: The Nyquist criterion requires that, when the closed loop is stable, the net winding number of the open-loop frequency response around -1+j0 must match the number P of open-loop right-half-plane poles according to the corresponding sign convention; if it does not match, then the closed loop has right-half-plane poles and is unstable. The winding number of System1 is consistent with P=1, so it is stable. The winding number of System2 is inconsistent with P=1, so the closed loop is unstable. The net winding number of System3 is consistent with P=0, so it is stable. Therefore only System (2) is an unstable system.

raw_record.question_text: The open-loop frequency response is shown in the figure. Which system is unstable?

method.method_draft: First describe the figure as three Nyquist/open-loop frequency-response curves labeled System 1, System 2, and System 3, each drawn relative to the real-axis point -1 and with frequency-direction arrows. For each system, read the plotted encirclement behavior and the given P/ν annotations. Then apply the Nyquist criterion to compare the encirclement of -1+j0 with the open-loop unstable-pole count. The comparison identifies only System (2) as violating the stability condition, so the unstable system is System (2).
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中并排给出三个开环频率响应/Nyquist 曲线，分别标为 System1、System2、System3。每幅图都有复平面坐标轴，横轴上标出关键实轴点 -1 和 0，并用箭头标明频率方向。System1 的标注为 P=1、ν=0，曲线从负实轴附近出发，向下绕成一段弧形后趋向 0；按完整 Nyquist 曲线看，它对 -1 点给出与 P=1 相匹配的 encirclement。System2 的标注为 P=1、ν=1，曲线在虚轴附近并向左弯曲，但相对于 -1 点的绕行情况没有满足 P=1 时所需的 Nyquist 绕数。System3 的标注为 P=0、ν=1，曲线在 -1 附近呈波形穿行，但净绕数为 0，与 P=0 相匹配。
再推理：Nyquist 判据要求闭环稳定时，开环频率响应对 -1+j0 的净绕数必须与开环右半平面极点数 P 按相应符号约定相匹配；若不匹配，则闭环存在右半平面极点而不稳定。System1 的绕数与 P=1 一致，因此稳定。System2 的绕数与 P=1 不一致，因此闭环不稳定。System3 的净绕数与 P=0 一致，因此稳定。所以只有 System (2) 是不稳定系统。
